convmoment

convmoment implements the generalized binomial framework for transforming statistical moments of any order across arbitrary origins (Mahmud, 2025). It provides a unified, exact, and computationally efficient method for:

  • Raw-to-Raw transformations across arbitrary origins
  • Raw-to-Central transformations (moments about origin to central moments about the mean)
  • Central-to-Raw transformations (central moments back to raw moments about )
  • Direct Moment Computation from sample data up to degree

The underlying mathematical identity uses the symbolic binomial operator:

![ \mu’_r(k) \equiv (a + b)^r = \sum_{j=0}^r \binom{r}{j} \mu’_j(a) \, b^{r-j}](https://latex.codecogs.com/png.image?%5Cdpi%7B110%7D&space;%5Cbg_white&space;%20%5Cmu%27_r%28k%29%20%5Cequiv%20%28a%20%2B%20b%29%5Er%20%3D%20%5Csum_%7Bj%3D0%7D%5Er%20%5Cbinom%7Br%7D%7Bj%7D%20%5Cmu%27_j%28a%29%20%5C%2C%20b%5E%7Br-j%7D%20 ” \mu’r(k) \equiv (a + b)^r = \sum{j=0}^r \binom{r}{j} \mu’_j(a) \, b^{r-j} “)

where is the origin-shift parameter and .

Installation

You can install the released version of convmoment from CRAN (once accepted) with:

install.packages("convmoment")

Or install the development version from GitHub using pak:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("mahmudstat/convmoment")

Key Functions

Function Description
conv_moment_all(x, a, k) Convert a vector of raw moments (orders ) from origin to target origin
raw2central(raw_moments, origin) Convert raw moments about origin to central moments (about the mean)
central2raw(central_moments, mean_val) Convert central moments to raw moments about origin
get_moments(x, a, r, na_rm, decimal) Compute raw or central moments directly from sample data up to degree

Examples

1. Raw-to-Raw Transformation Across Origins

Suppose the raw moments of a variable about origin are , , and . What are the raw moments about origin ?

library(convmoment)

# Raw moments about origin a = 2
x <- c(1, 16, -40)

# Convert to origin k = 0
conv_moment_all(x, a = 2, k = 0)
#> [1]  3 24 76

2. Raw-to-Central and Central-to-Raw Conversions

Convert raw moments about 0 to central moments (about the mean) and perform a round-trip check:

set.seed(42)
data <- rnorm(200, mean = 10, sd = 3)

# Compute raw moments about 0 (orders 1..5)
raw_m <- sapply(1:5, function(r) mean(data^r))

# Convert raw moments to central moments
central_m <- raw2central(raw_m, origin = 0)
central_m
#> [1]    0.000000    8.505605   -3.469533  224.557258 -305.155626

# Round-trip back to raw moments
raw_reconstructed <- central2raw(central_m, mean_val = mean(data))
all.equal(raw_m, raw_reconstructed)
#> [1] TRUE

3. Compute Moments Directly from Sample Data

Calculate raw moments around origin up to 4th order:

set.seed(123)
sample_data <- rnorm(100, mean = 5, sd = 2)

# Compute moments about origin a = 2 up to order r = 4
get_moments(sample_data, a = 2, r = 4, decimal = 4)
#>   Order   Moment
#> 1     1   3.1808
#> 2     2  13.4172
#> 3     3  64.0309
#> 4     4 338.1910
